newsitem.title: USA: Maine, Rhode Island file tobacco suits.
newsitem.headline: Maine, Rhode Island file tobacco suits.

text.p: Maine and Rhode Island Wednesday became the 39th and 40th states to sue the tobacco industry seeking to recover the costs of providing health care to smokers.
The lawsuits, each filed in state court, mean that only 10 states have not gone to court against cigarette makers.
The Maine and Rhode Island suits both seek reimbursement of state Medicaid costs for treating smoking-related illness and also ask for unspecified punitive damages.
Maine estimated smoking-related illnesses cost its Medicaid programme $50 million a year. An estimate on Rhode Island's costs was not immediately available.
Maine also wants a mandatory curb on tobacco advertising aimed at children. An estimated 32 percent of Maine residents age 18 to 30 are smokers, giving it the nation's highest youth smoking rate.
"If you simply do the math, one in nine current Maine children will die because of tobacco-related illness," Maine Attorney General Andrew Ketterer told reporters.
